answer_1.quote: Automatic story generation aims to produce interesting stories to be read by readers or help writers develop new ideas.
answer_1.outputs: Generated story bodies and their endings

answer_2.quote: We use the next sentence prediction (NSP) task of BERT to measure the coherence between the story and the ending... we use the perplexity score as another metric to measure the story ending's quality... we measure intra-story lexical diversity using self-BLEU and within-story lexical diversity (or repetition) using distinct-n.

answer_3.quote: During inference, we sample multiple (story body, story ending) pairs and use NSP and PPL to rank them.

answer_4.quote: We generate 50 stories using each model and invite three crowdworkers to evaluate each story on the following fine-grained aspects: naturalness, interestingness, and cohesiveness.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were asked to rate each story on naturalness, interestingness, and cohesiveness, and in pairwise comparisons to choose which ending is better.
